chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja'far, who said:

Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) wrote to Abu al-Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja'far al-Zubayri about twenty days before the death of al-Mu'tazz: "Remain in your house until the event occurs." Then, when Burayhah was killed, he wrote to him: "The event has occurred, so what do you order me to do?" He wrote back: "This is not the event; it is the other event." Then there occurred, regarding al-Mu'tazz, what occurred.
And from him, he said: He wrote to another man: "The son of Muhammad ibn Dawud, 'Abd Allah, will be killed," ten days before his killing. Then, when the tenth day came, he was killed.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, the appellation of Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام)
key_terms.الْمُعْتَزِّ: al-Mu'tazz, the Abbasid caliph referred to in the report
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الْعَاشِرِ: the tenth day, marking the exact fulfillment of the report
key_terms.بُرَيْحَةُ: Burayhah, whose killing prompted the inquiry
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: will be killed; a prediction of impending death

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi say about Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) foretelling the fall of al-Mu'tazz?
ai.summary: This narration reports foreknowledge conveyed by Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) concerning political upheaval and the death of specific individuals. It highlights the Imam's precise indication of coming events and situates his correspondence within the historical context of the fall of al-Mu'tazz.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Ibrahim Bin Musa Bin Ja’far who said,

Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) wrote to my father Al-Qasim Is’haq Bin Ja’far Al-Zubeyri before the death of Al-Mu’taz (the Caliph) by approximately twenty days: ‘Stay in your house until the event occurs’. So when Bureyha was killed, he wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>: ‘The event has occurred, so what are you<sup>asws</sup> ordering me with?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘This is not the event. It is another event’. So when it was from the matter of Al-Mu’taz what was’.
And from him who said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> wrote to another man: ‘He would be killed, Ibn Muhammad Bin Dawood Abdullah’, ten days before he was killed. So when it was the tenth day, he was killed’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Once abu Muhammad (a.s.) wrote to abu al-Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja‘far al-Zubayri before the death of al-Mu‘tazz by about twenty days as herein below. ‘Stay home until what is to happen will happen.’ When Burayha was killed he wrote to him, “A happening has happened. What would you command me to do?” He wrote back, “This is not the happening. It is another happening.” Then there was the case of al-Mu‘tazz the way it was.”

It is narrated from the same narrator that the Imam (a.s.) wrote to another person. “Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn ‘Abdallah will be killed.” It was ten days before his murder. On the tenth day he was killed.”
